answers.question: What is the scavenge air pressure at full load?
answers.expected_fact: 2.4 bar
answers.answer: According to Document 1, index "1", title "Main Engine Operation", the scavenge air pressure at full load is 2.4 bar. [1]

answers.question: At what lubricating oil pressure does the main engine shut down automatically?
answers.expected_fact: 2.2 bar
answers.answer: According to document [1], the automatic shutdown of the main engine occurs at 2.2 bar.

answers.question: What is the auxiliary boiler working pressure?
answers.expected_fact: 7 bar
answers.answer: The auxiliary boiler working pressure is 7 bar. [1]

answers.question: What jacket cooling water outlet temperature is maintained at the main engine?
answers.expected_fact: eighty-five degrees Celsius
answers.answer: The jacket cooling water outlet temperature from the main engine is maintained at eighty-five degrees Celsius. [1]

answers.question: How long is the bunker sample retained on board after delivery?
answers.expected_fact: twelve months
answers.answer: The provided documents do not cover that.

answers.question: Within how long must the emergency generator connect to the emergency switchboard after a blackout?
answers.expected_fact: forty-five seconds
answers.answer: According to document [1], "On loss of main electrical power the emergency generator starts automatically and connects to the emergency switchboard within forty-five seconds."

answers.question: What temperature does the fuel oil purifier run at, and how many running hours between overhauls?
answers.expected_fact: ninety-eight degrees Celsius, overhauled every 2000 running hours
answers.answer: According to document [1], the fuel oil purifier operates at a temperature of ninety-eight degrees Celsius. The interval for overhaul is every 2000 running hours.

answers.question: What is the chloride limit for boiler water and what is it for the closed jacket cooling circuit?
answers.expected_fact: boiler water 100 ppm, jacket cooling water 50 ppm
answers.answer: According to the provided documents, [1], the chloride limit for boiler water is 100 parts per million. In contrast, the chloride limit for the closed jacket cooling circuit is 50 parts per million.

answers.question: Which is kept on board longer, the Oil Record Book or the Ballast Water Record Book?
answers.expected_fact: Oil Record Book three years; Ballast Water Record Book two years on board
answers.answer: The Oil Record Book is retained on board for three years from the date of the last entry, whereas the Ballast Water Record Book is retained on board for two years from the date of the last entry. Therefore, the Oil Record Book is kept on board longer than the Ballast Water Record Book. [1]

answers.question: How often is the emergency generator tested and what must it achieve when it starts?
answers.expected_fact: run on load monthly; must connect within forty-five seconds
answers.answer: The emergency generator is run on load monthly. When it starts automatically on loss of main power, it must connect to the emergency switchboard within forty-five seconds.

answers.question: If we keep the ship going very slowly for a long time, how low can the power be set before it stops being allowed?
answers.expected_fact: fifteen per cent of maximum continuous rating
answers.answer: The provided documents do not cover that.

answers.question: How often does someone working alone down in the machinery space have to show they are still all right?
answers.expected_fact: reset at intervals not exceeding thirty minutes
answers.answer: According to document [1], while the space is unattended and an engineer is working within it, the personnel alarm system is activated. The engineer must reset the system at intervals not exceeding thirty minutes. Failure to reset raises a pre-alarm in the space and, if still unanswered, a general alarm on the bridge and in the accommodation.

answers.question: How much oil can be left in the water before we are not allowed to pump it over the side?
answers.expected_fact: 15 parts per million
answers.answer: According to the provided documents, oily mixture from machinery space bilges may be discharged to sea only through approved filtering equipment and only when the oil content of the effluent does not exceed 15 parts per million.

answers.question: How much oil is put onto the cylinder walls for each unit of power the engine makes?
answers.expected_fact: 0.8 grams per kilowatt hour
answers.answer: According to document [1], the feed rate of cylinder oil is set to 0.8 grams per kilowatt hour at normal service load.

answers.question: If we have to swap the water in the tanks the old way at sea, how far from shore do we need to be?
answers.expected_fact: at least two hundred nautical miles from the nearest land
answers.answer: According to the provided documents, if exchange is used as a contingency measure where the treatment system is inoperative and the alternative arrangements have been agreed, it must be carried out at least 200 nautical miles from the nearest land.

answers.question: What does the D-2 standard require?
answers.expected_fact: fewer than ten viable organisms per cubic metre of fifty micrometres or greater
answers.answer: According to the first document, the D-2 standard requires that discharged ballast water must contain fewer than ten viable organisms per cubic metre that are fifty micrometres or greater in minimum dimension, and fewer than ten viable organisms per millilitre that are between ten and fifty micrometres.

answers.question: What is the gravity disc selected for?
answers.expected_fact: the density of the fuel in service
answers.answer: The gravity disc is fitted to the fuel oil purifier and is selected for the density of the fuel in service. [1]

answers.question: What is the cascade tank and what is it watched for?
answers.expected_fact: condensate returns there and it is observed for oil contamination
answers.answer:
The cascade tank is mentioned in two documents as a container where condensate returns to before being returned to the boiler. It is also mentioned that oil reaches the cascade tank through a leaking heating coil in a fuel or sludge tank.

According to document 3, the cascade tank is watched for oil contamination, which can prevent heat transfer to the water and cause overheating locally.

answers.question: What is the critical speed range of the shaft line?
answers.expected_fact: between forty-two and fifty-eight revolutions per minute
answers.answer: According to the provided documents, the critical speed range of the shaft line is between 42 and 58 revolutions per minute. [1] This band is marked on the bridge and engine room telegraph repeaters, and the engine must be accelerated through this band without dwelling in it, and continuous running inside the band is prohibited under any circumstance.

answers.question: Is it ever permitted to run continuously inside the critical speed range?
answers.expected_fact: No — prohibited under any circumstance
answers.answer: According to the provided documents, sustained operation within the resonance band (critical speed range) is prohibited under any circumstance, including during manoeuvring, trials, and astern running.

answers.question: Can sludge be discharged to sea if its oil content is below the 15 ppm limit?
answers.expected_fact: No — sludge is not discharged to sea under any circumstance
answers.answer: The provided documents do not cover that.

answers.question: Does the fifty degree exhaust deviation rule apply to the turbocharger inlet temperature?
answers.expected_fact: No — it is not subject to the fifty-degree deviation rule
answers.answer: The provided documents state that the fifty-degree deviation rule applies to single cylinder readings from the mean of all cylinders. However, it is explicitly mentioned that the turbocharger inlet temperature is a separate measurement and is not subject to this rule because it is a mixed temperature drawn from all cylinders and has no per-cylinder mean to deviate from.

answers.question: Is water washing the turbine side the correct response to turbocharger surge?
answers.expected_fact: No — washing is a routine interval task, not a response to surge
answers.answer: According to document [1], "Turbocharger turbine side water washing is carried out every 250 running hours." It also states that "Washing a surging machine at load will not clear the condition and may crack the nozzle ring through thermal shock." This implies that water washing of the turbine side is not a response to turbocharger surge.
